epic.title: program(perf): facade cost model, sync-getter mirrors, compat-overhead benchmark lane, channel-id allocation rule and parallelism plan
epic.body:
## Scope
How compatibility and performance meet: every Electron main-process call that is synchronous in Electron and needs host state becomes a facade mirror read (zero traffic), a write-through Call, or a documented ▲; renderer→main hops double versus Electron; the kipc client cannot block today (panel); measurement rules from arch 01 §5/§5.1.

## Measured today (never blended with targets)
Windows host-process RSS 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (Electron won total process tree); host-only first paint Keld 469 / Tauri 479 / Electron 275 ms (Electron leads); Windows kipc Bun↔Rust diagnostic p99 ≈ 101 µs (1 session, not publication-eligible); macOS Rust↔Rust library arm p99 ≈ 9.3–9.6 µs; Bun extension-host bootstrap PoC 53% sooner (narrow). Forbidden claims are listed on the map.

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2; X05-A1/A3 settled by the panel)
- Window-state mirror: host events stamped with a monotonic per-window state generation; getters read the mirror synchronously, setters are write-through; zero steady-state allocation per read.
- The KEL-142 one-pending floor blocks Zettlr at L1 (186 invoke sites): floor v2 (F04-T2) is a hard prerequisite for ipcRenderer.invoke.
- Hot-path cost model: Keld webContents.send = facade serialisation → kipc frame → host routing → engine script evaluation into the isolated world (≥ 3 serialise stages vs Electron's 2); per-frame allocation exists today in the TS reader/writer and the Rust frame read.
- Benchmark lane: same-app compat-overhead arms in gyldlab/keld-benches (electron-quick-start first, then draw.io), registered metric ids FACADE-RTT (renderer invoke → ipcMain.handle → reply), FACADE-DELTA (`@keld/electron` minus raw `@keld/api`), SEND-FANOUT, SYNC-BLOCK, plus the §5.1 product census (idle RSS, first paint) with interleaved rounds, ≥20 sessions × 100k calls for IPC.
- Serial step 0: a channel-id and capability-name allocation rule (reserved id ranges per family, generated constants) because every family touches the same hand-mirrored constants in keld-ipc and the TS transport.

verdict.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel transport/schema/policy owner; reuse of Linear owners; unmeasured perf decides nothing; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127). Verified against keld origin/main b4b907c3, GitHub gyldlab/keld issues, and live Linear team KELD (read-only, fetched 2026-10-06; no Linear call failed; no writes made).

verdicts.reason: The core decision (host-authoritative, generation-stamped facade mirror for Electron-synchronous window getters) is forced by evidence and adds no fifth unique, transport, or policy owner: state events can ride the existing app-link EVENT kind the lifecycle channel already uses. The rejected alternatives are confirmed dead: a blocking CALL per getter is unavailable (the shipped Bun kipc client cannot block) and async getters break the first-proof corpus. It survives only with four corrections, because the write-through half and one perf sentence are not supported.
verdicts.evidence: FACT draw.io corpus src/main/electron.js:824-832 rememberWinSize reads win.getSize(), getPosition(), isMaximized(), isFullScreen() synchronously into store.set. FACT docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md:321 'no UI thread blocks on Bun, app-link I/O, or handler completion'. FACT crates/keld-core/src has no WindowRegistry (grep 0); only LifecycleSession::window_opened/window_closed (lifecycle.rs:133,143). FACT crates/keld-wv/AGENTS.md:6 'Engine/window mutations MUST stay on tao UI thread'. FACT KEL-127 comment 2026-10-06 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): 'the shipped Bun kipc client cannot block (#422), and a parked Bun main thread stalls the only link after 8 KiB (probe)'. FACT packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts FrameKind.Event=4 and LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL=3 already carry host-to-Bun events; arch 02 says the lifecycle wire names 'are host-lifecycle, not Electron-isms'. FACT Linear list (fetched 2026-10-06): no issue owns a window registry; nearest window owners are KEL-25 (In Progress) and children KEL-26/27/28; KEL-233 (Done) owns recovered-generation window event replay.
verdicts.correction: (1) Delete 'zero allocation per read' and 'removes nearly all round trips': unmeasured, and getBounds must return a fresh Rectangle per call or app mutation corrupts the mirror. (2) Write-through makes the facade a second writer of host-owned window state: specify that an optimistic value is provisional, is rolled back on CALL ERR (a guard denial produces no confirming event, so 'reconciled by the confirming event' leaves a permanent lie), and that after Bun generation recovery the mirror is rebuilt from a host snapshot through the existing replay owner (KEL-233 artifact, KEL-143 ordering) before any getter answers. (3) Name the owner: no Linear issue owns the window registry; window handles stay with keld-wv on the UI thread, keld-core gets only generic window-state facts (no Electron names in keld-core/keld-ipc); moving handle ownership would be an architecture change needing an approved spec. (4) The A1 'unknown' about a synchronous Bun socket read is now resolved on the map (#422) and should be cited as the reason alternative (a) is dead, not left unknown.

verdicts.reason: The contract half (same guarded channel, absolute deadline, compat-config rate limit, dev warning, thrown error on deadline, explicit diagnosed divergence instead of a silent Promise) is consistent with arch 02 section 5, arch 04 and KEL-127. The mechanism half is not decidable from current evidence, and the proposed prototype omits the decision-bearing identity atom: the WKWebView sync-XHR path is a second renderer-to-host route whose handler receives no frame or content-world identity. Two stated facts are also wrong in attribution or admissibility. draw.io has zero sendSync sites, so this is parked for the first proof either way.
verdicts.evidence: FACT KEL-127 description (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06) says only 'Async-first native APIs do not authorize pretending asynchronous calls preserve synchronous Electron semantics' and 'A silent asynchronous replacement changes the caller contract'; it does not contain 'must stay blocking', 'rate-limited' or 'dev-warned'. FACT that wording is docs/architecture/02-ipc.md:336-337 ('sync sendSync supported but rate-limited + dev-warned (it's a blocking CALL with a deadline; ... so it must exist)') and docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md:24,39. FACT KEL-142 description (Linear, Done 2026-10-01): 'It must not create a second renderer-routing protocol' and 'Page cannot read endpoint/token ... forge principal/generation, or access preload realm'. FACT Apple WKURLSchemeTask JSON (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/webkit/wkurlschemetask.json, retrieved 2026-10-06) exposes only request, didReceive, didFinish, didFailWithError: no frame, no content world. INFERENCE therefore page-world script can issue the same sync XHR as the isolated compat world and the host cannot tell them apart without an extra binding. FACT KEL-127 comment 2026-09-17 records WebView2 callbacks as UI-thread-affine; INFERENCE a hostObjects.sync call must return its value from a host COM method on the UI thread, so the host UI thread would block on Bun, which A2's own rejected alternative (c) and kel142:321 forbid; host objects are also exposed to the page main world, contradicting A2's own security mapping. FACT draw.io corpus: ipcRenderer usage is on x3, once x1, send x2, sendSync x0; Zettlr sendSync x6 (verified paths). FACT KEL-79 (scheme/resource transport owner) is Backlog (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).
verdicts.correction: Missing evidence: (a) whether a sync XHR to a WKURLSchemeHandler scheme blocks web content on the pinned WebKit and what it does at the deadline; (b) whether the host can bind that request to the isolated compat world and current navigation generation. Cheapest discriminating experiment: extend the existing scratchpad probe wayfinder/electron-compat/probes/f05-wk-scheme (it already registers a WKURLSchemeHandler) with one sync XHR from page script and one from a WKContentWorld user script, host completing after a configurable delay; observe blocking, deadline outcome, and whether the handler can distinguish the two callers. Negative controls required before any spec: page-world and iframe requests are refused, stale-navigation requests are refused. Also: re-attribute the blocking/rate-limit wording to arch 02 section 5 and arch 04; drop the blocker 'KEL-127 owner confirmation that an async-only cell satisfies must-stay-blocking' (KEL-127 and KEL-98 already require explicit diagnosis, not blocking) and replace it with 'arch 02 section 5 says sendSync must exist; an async-only cell needs that spec sentence changed in the same PR'; strike hostObjects.sync as an admissible Windows mechanism (the Windows candidate is the same sync-XHR shape with deferred resource completion, unproven); route any resulting spec through KEL-79 + KEL-80 with wire-protocol and permission-model gates.

verdicts.reason: The answer 'No' is correct on primary evidence and the owner routing is right: KEL-142 is explicitly the narrow first slice of KEL-80 and KEL-80 is the unstarted owner of bounded multi-pending and backpressure. It actually binds the first proof harder than stated, through a path the decision did not name. Four corrections on framing, none of which changes the verdict.
verdicts.evidence: FACT docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md:125-127 'Exactly one renderer-originated invoke may be pending per WebView in this minimum slice. A second invoke while the first is pending fails immediately; there is no hidden unbounded queue', :313 'no second renderer CALL is admitted while one is pending', and :30,:133,:479 the slice ships no send/on/stream. FACT KEL-142 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): Done 2026-10-01, parent KEL-139, 'narrow first product slice of KEL-80's ... contract', blocks KEL-140/143/144. FACT KEL-80 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): Backlog, unassigned, no blockers, acceptance already lists host-enforced credits, per-channel ordering, one terminal caller outcome, and 'WriteQueue has no aggregate pending-call/byte limit'; no docs/specs/kel80-* file exists. FACT Zettlr corpus: 186 ipcRenderer.invoke matches. FACT draw.io corpus: 0 invoke, but electron-preload.js:102 sends 'rendererReq' and :61 listens for 'mainResp', with electron.js:4431/4537 replying by reqId, i.e. app-level concurrent request/response over one-way send plus event.reply. FACT a grep for Promise.all wrapping ipcRenderer.invoke in Zettlr returned 0.
verdicts.correction: (1) For the first proof the binding gap is one-way renderer-to-main send plus host-routed event back to the sender webview (draw.io's rendererReq/mainResp), which KEL-142 does not ship; multi-pending invoke is the Zettlr (second workload) requirement. Order the KEL-80 slice that way. (2) Relabel 'Vue components issue overlapping invokes during mount' from fact to inference; the peak-concurrency census already listed is the evidence. (3) Remove '186 calls at ~50-100 us each': it multiplies static call sites by a Windows diagnostic that is not publication-eligible; correctness alone decides this. (4) Replace 'KEL-142 section 6 amendment' with a new KEL-80 slice spec (KEL-142 is Done and its rule is scoped 'in this minimum slice'), carrying wire-protocol and public-API gates, and starting from KEL-80's recorded first action (producer/queue ownership ledger and bounded slow-consumer regression) before any bound is chosen. (5) 'BEHAVIOR_MATCH' is not KEL-74 vocabulary (see extra finding).

verdicts.reason: The honest-status rule (the live path allocates per frame; no allocation-free claim until an attributed lane shows it) and the 'measure before design' typing are directly supported by code and specs, and the decision correctly refuses the unmeasured '10x faster' claim, batching, and shared memory. Two of its five rules misstate the existing owners and must be corrected.
verdicts.evidence: FACT packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts:432 copies each chunk, :471 and :591 copy out each payload, :831 allocates header+payload per write. FACT crates/keld-ipc/src/link.rs:188,224,244 'let mut payload = vec![0u8; len]'; receive.rs:17 validator is 'synchronous, allocation-free'. FACT docs/architecture/02-ipc.md:341-344 zero-allocation and single-producer-queue text sits under destination hot-path rules. FACT research notes 101 and 163 exist in the nested research checkout. FACT crates/keld-runtime/src/virtual_port.rs:15 MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN = 4096. FACT docs/architecture/02-ipc.md section 5 maps 'webContents.send' to a 'host-routed EVENT to a specific webview principal' and maps only MessagePorts to virtual-port pairs. FACT KEL-80 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): '4 KiB is the present virtual-port inline ceiling; 1 MiB/16 MiB arms belong only to protocols that actually admit them'. FACT transport.ts:856-900 WriteQueue is an unbounded promise chain with only a per-frame length check; KEL-80 acceptance requires 'one authoritative budget for pending bytes AND calls'.
verdicts.correction: (1) Rule 5 and the related security-mapping row conflate two routes: webContents.send is a host-routed EVENT, not a virtual-port message, so the 4096-byte ceiling does not apply to it; applying it would break draw.io replies that carry file data. State the webContents.send payload bound as unknown, to be set by the KEL-80 slice (frame cap and engine-injection cap), and keep 4096 for MessagePortMain only. (2) Rule 2 ('the kipc WriteQueue is the only queue') relies on a queue that has no aggregate bound today; a main-process loop of webContents.send therefore inherits a hidden unbounded queue. Make the rule conditional on KEL-80's admission budget and add a slow-consumer negative control. (3) Label the Electron-side model (structured clone plus one Mojo hop) as inference; only the throw-on-unserializable sentence has a receipt. (4) The repository's allocation-free rule governs Rust kipc/event-loop/guard paths; a TypeScript structured-clone facade cannot be allocation-free, so the ticket title should say 'bounded and attributed', not 'allocation-free rules for facade hot paths'.

verdicts.reason: The plan reuses the correct owners and refuses every blended or ineligible claim, and its one stated ownership unknown is now resolved in its favour by live Linear. It survives with corrections because its blocker list is incomplete, it is not needed by the first-proof milestone, and one cited authority is an untracked file.
verdicts.evidence: FACT KEL-127 description (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): 'KEL-90 owns matched full-application measurements without replacing KEL-129's budget authority'. FACT KEL-90: In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB; its acceptance requires 'generated-app functional lifecycle fidelity and independently attributed complete process/engine census before a comparative metric is admitted', 'at least 30 balanced independent launches', comparator mode tags, reuse of result.v2 and the existing metric registry ('not a second benchmarking system'), and 'A comparator crash, unsupported operation or correctness divergence invalidates that sample'. FACT KEL-129: In Progress, parent KEL-127; KEL-99: Done. FACT docs/engineering/budget-scoreboard.md rows verified: 19,552 KB vs 89,140 KB 'does not mean lower total application RSS'; 469/479/275 ms host-only diagnostic; KEL-99 'publication.eligible is false'. FACT packages/@keld/electron/src contains only app.ts and link.ts (no BrowserWindow, ipcMain). FACT keld-benches README (gh api, retrieved 2026-10-06): 'This repo is fixtures only', lanes PAINT-OPPORTUNITY/MEM-IDLE/DISK, Electron comparator is 43.4.0 hello. FACT draw.io package.json:52 pins electron ^44.2.0. FACT 'Electron Compatibility Reference for KELD.md' is untracked (git status ??); its line 1307 is the only source of 'must never be blended'; tracked budget-scoreboard.md:107 says 'never blend' about split lanes only. FACT KEL-127: 'Budget feasibility is a parallel decision rail ... must not be used to claim current product readiness'.
verdicts.correction: (1) Change the KEL-90 ownership item from unknown to fact with the Linear receipt. (2) Add the missing blockers: the Keld arm of the quick-start lane needs BrowserWindow and page load to exist in the facade, and FACADE-RTT needs ipcMain/ipcRenderer; only registering metric ids and defining the Electron arm is startable now, so the published 'ready-for-agent' label on the lane ticket should be narrowed to that. (3) A quick-start 'with one echo channel' is a modified fixture, not corpus app electron-quick-start@82dbb35; name it as a fixture with its own digest. (4) Use each app's lockfile-resolved Electron for its Electron arm, or record the delta from 44.4.5; existing cited comparisons were against Electron 43.4.0. (5) Adopt KEL-90's admission gates (lifecycle fidelity first, 30 balanced launches for launch-shaped metrics, mode tags) alongside the kipc census. (6) Park the lane behind the first proof: the milestone ships correctly without it. (7) Re-anchor the three-claim-class rule on a tracked owner (KEL-86/KEL-90 rules and the budget scoreboard) or land it there; an untracked reference file is not an authority.

FACT docs/specs/kel98-echo-codegen.md section 4: the generated file 'contains no ... channel table, or transport logic' and 'Wire/protocol changes: none ... channel numbers ... remain unchanged'. FACT KEL-98 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): Done 2026-09-20; 'Preserve this issue's original smallest echo-codegen slice'; 'Introduce no new wire version/opcode until the owning contract review requires it'. FACT GitHub #319 (closed): 'Migration breadth consumes those primitives and should follow them rather than compete with them for execution capacity ... no migration implementation is authorized here'. FACT GitHub #312 (closed): 'KELD-native vertical slice -> Electron migration proof -> broader developer distribution polish'; 'does not authorize broad native APIs, full Electron compatibility'. FACT KEL-127 description (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06) non-goals: 'No shared memory, CEF, broad Electron API expansion, additional native-module names, or updater implementation before G2'; 'Preserve the existing small concurrency budget'. FACT Linear statuses fetched 2026-10-06: KEL-140, KEL-141, KEL-143, KEL-144 Backlog; KEL-102 In Progress; KEL-79 and KEL-80 Backlog; KEL-53 In Progress; KEL-142 and KEL-139 Done. FACT docs/agents/workflow.md:197 'Budget: 3-7 agents, disjoint crates'. FACT nine families exist (F01..F09) but the six tracks omit F03 webcontents-navigation and F07 renderer/webview-tag.
verdicts.correction: (1) Replace step 0 with: an approved spec for the minimum slice of the arch 02 section 4 channel table (schema name to u16 at handshake, capability declared with the channel), owned by keld-ipc with wire-protocol, permission-model and public-API gates; it also retires the three existing hand copies. No per-Electron-family id ranges in keld-ipc: Electron channels are app-chosen strings and travel as data under the already-resolved enumerated per-window el:<channel> grant, so families do not each consume a kipc channel id. KEL-98 is Done and its spec excludes a channel table; cite it as the pattern, not the generator owner. (2) Replace 'T-A/T-B/T-E do not need the spine to start' with per-track entry gates on task-level artifacts: T-A on KEL-102/T3 plus KEL-140 (the guarded-operation pattern), T-B on a window-owner spec (no Linear owner exists), T-C on a KEL-80 slice spec plus KEL-143 ordering, T-D on KEL-79, T-E on KEL-53 full-package activation and after G2 per the KEL-127 non-goal. Until those land only zero-authority work runs: conformance entries, Electron-oracle fixtures, scratchpad prototypes. (3) Correct the reading of #319: it orders migration breadth after the spine and names execution capacity as the reason; overriding that is an owner decision. research.summary: Answer to "backward compatibility AND better performance, faster": compatibility is bought by cloning Electron's observable contract in a TS facade over kipc, and performance is bought by what the facade does NOT ship (bundled Chromium, Electron main-process stack). The two meet at one cost model: every Electron main-process call that is synchronous in Electron and needs host state becomes either (i) a blocking CALL (one kipc round trip, Windows Bun<->Rust diagnostic p50 ~47 us / p99 ~101 us vs 100 us budget, not publication-eligible; macOS/Linux Bun arm unmeasured; Rust<->Rust macOS library arm p99 9.25-9.6 us), (ii) a facade-side state mirror answered synchronously and kept coherent by host events carrying a generation/sequence stamp (write-through on setters), or (iii) an async-only divergence (▲) that changes the caller contract. Evidence says: [fact] the corpus does use sync getters in time-critical paths (draw.io persists getSize/getPosition/isMaximized/isFullScreen inside a close handler; 6 isDestroyed guards), [fact] Zettlr has 6 sendSync sites and 186 ipcRenderer.invoke sites, [fact] KEL-142's live minimum renderer bridge admits exactly one pending invoke per WebView, so the ipcRenderer facade cannot reach L1 for Zettlr until bounded multi-pending correlation (KEL-80 owner) exists. What gets cheaper is measured only narrowly: [fact] 78% lower main-process RSS in one Windows direct-COM session (total RSS NOT lower there), [fact] Bun bootstrap 53.3% sooner / 42.8% lower RSS in a narrow VS Code extension-host PoC, while [fact] Electron led first paint 275 ms vs Keld 469 ms (Chromium controller-creation floor, KEL-62). No compat-overhead lane exists in gyldlab/keld-benches (README fetched 2026-10-06), so facade cost today is a model, not a measurement; the plan is a same-app Electron-vs-Keld lane under KEL-90/KEL-129 census rules with p50/p95/p99 block-bootstrap and three never-blended claim classes (measured / target / projection). "Faster" delivery comes from parallelizing families that own disjoint crates/packages (native-desktop brokers, windowing registry+mirror, updater adapter, session/protocol transport) after one small serial step: a single-owner kipc channel-id and guard capability-name allocation rule, because keld-ipc frame constants, @keld/kipc transport.ts mirror constants, keld-guard manifest schema, Cargo.toml and root AGENTS.md are single-writer files that every family would otherwise collide on. Conformance entries and fixtures for every Tier 1 family can start now with zero code collision. "Faster" MUST NOT mean skipping conformance entries, widening permissions, retries, sleeps, a Rust rewrite as proof, blending claim classes, or publishing a percentage without a committed denominator.

decisions.question: How do Electron-synchronous main-process window getters (getBounds/getSize/getPosition/isMaximized/isFullScreen/isDestroyed/getFocusedWindow/getAllWindows) get implemented without either lying (stale) or blocking the Bun event loop on every read?
decisions.proposed_answer: Facade-side window-state mirror, host-authoritative: the host (keld-core window registry, TARGET) emits window-state events (bounds, maximize/unmaximize, fullscreen, focus, destroyed) over the app link, each stamped with a monotonic per-window state generation. Getters read the mirror synchronously (zero kipc traffic, zero allocation per read). Setters (setBounds/maximize/...) are write-through: the facade applies the requested value to the mirror and issues the CALL; the host's confirming event (with the new generation) reconciles or corrects it, and a correction emits the Electron-visible event ('resize'/'move'). isDestroyed() and the 'Object has been destroyed' throw are answered purely from the mirror's destroyed flag, set by the host's destroyed event and by local destroy(). Divergence to record as ▲: between an OS-initiated change and arrival of the host event the getter can be one generation stale; Electron reads Chromium's in-process view so it is never stale. [inference] Reads dominate writes in the corpus (draw.io: 6 isDestroyed, 3 isFullScreen, 2 isMaximized, getSize/getPosition in a 'close' handler; Zettlr: 3 isMaximized, 3 getSize, 2 getBounds, 7 'resize' listeners), so the mirror removes nearly all round trips from these paths.
evidence: [fact] Electron v44.4.5 browser-window.md: getBounds returns Rectangle; getSize/getPosition return Integer[]; isMaximized/isFullScreen/isDestroyed return boolean (synchronous); 'Reading this property throws Object has been destroyed once the window has been destroyed' (retrieved 2026-10-06)

[fact] drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:828-830 reads win.getSize(), win.getPosition(), win.isMaximized(), win.isFullScreen() synchronously to persist lastWinSize; :107,:149,:902,:1419,:3216,:4375 guard with isDestroyed()

[fact] keld-core has no window registry type today (grep WindowRegistry = 0); briefing lists it TARGET

decisions.question: Can ipcRenderer.sendSync keep Electron's blocking-renderer contract on system webviews, as KEL-127 directs (blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned), or is async-only the only honest option?
decisions.proposed_answer: Treat it per engine and record each as its own scoreboard cell. [fact] Electron: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received, so use this method only as a last resort'; main sees it as the distinct 'ipc-message-sync' event. [fact] WebView2 (Chromium-derived) exposes chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.* synchronous proxies (Microsoft how-to page shows `chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.sample.dateProperty` usage), so a blocking renderer->host hop is available there. [fact] WKWebView's documented JS->native paths (WKScriptMessageHandler, WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply via window.webkit.messageHandlers.<name>.postMessage) are asynchronous; Apple's page describes no synchronous call path. [lead] The only known blocking emulation on WKWebView is a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a WKURLSchemeHandler-served custom scheme (renderer web-content process blocks while the host completes the task asynchronously); this is unverified in Keld and must be prototyped, including its deadline behavior and whether sync XHR is still permitted on the main thread in the pinned WebKit. [unknown] WebKitGTK path. decisions.question: Does the live renderer bridge (KEL-142: exactly one pending invoke per WebView, second invoke fails immediately) allow an ipcRenderer.invoke facade that real apps can use?
decisions.proposed_answer: No. [fact] Zettlr has 186 ipcRenderer.invoke call sites across 65 files and 25 ipcMain.handle sites; Vue components issue overlapping invokes during mount. decisions.question: What is the hot-path cost model for the chatty one-way patterns (webContents.send main->renderer; ipcRenderer.send renderer->main; window event fan-out), and which rules keep facade hot paths allocation-free and semantically honest?
decisions.proposed_answer: Model (per call): Electron webContents.send = structured clone + one Mojo hop, in-process on the main side, synchronous throw at the call site for Function/Promise/Symbol/WeakMap/WeakSet arguments. Keld webContents.send = facade serialization in Bun -> one kipc frame Bun->host (today: TS FrameReader/WriteQueue allocate per frame; Rust read_frame allocates one Vec per payload) -> host routes to the window-bound virtual channel -> engine postMessage/evaluateJavaScript into the isolated world -> page listener. So Keld adds one extra process hop versus Electron's main process but removes Electron's main-process Chromium stack; whether net latency is better is UNMEASURED. Rules: (1) serialization semantics are the contract: throw synchronously at the facade for the same type set Electron rejects; do not silently drop or JSON-null them; (2) one serialization, one frame, no second buffering layer in the facade (the kipc WriteQueue is the only queue; arch 02 §6 'per-link single-producer queues'); (3) event fan-out from host to many windows is host-side routing, never N facade CALLs; (4) the zero-steady-state-allocation rule is arch 02 §6's destination and is NOT met by the live code (research 101/163) - the facade MUST NOT be claimed allocation-free until the attributed allocation lane in keld-benches shows zero per CALL in both Bun and Rust arms; until then the honest status is 'bounded, per-frame allocating'; (5) payload bound: MAX_FRAME_LEN 16 MiB for frames, MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN 4096 for virtual ports - a webContents.send of a large object over a 4096-byte port path must fail with a typed error, not fragment silently.
